T1003.001.name: OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory
T1003.001.summary: Adversaries read the memory of lsass.exe to harvest credentials, e.g. via MiniDump (comsvcs.dll), procdump or custom tools.

T1059.001.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
T1059.001.summary: Abuse of PowerShell to execute commands, often with encoded commands (-enc) or hidden windows, frequently spawned from Office applications.

T1021.002.name: Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
T1021.002.summary: Use of SMB (tcp/445), admin shares, and service-based remote execution (PsExec-style PSEXESVC) to move between hosts.

T1021.006.name: Remote Services: Windows Remote Management
T1021.006.summary: WinRM (tcp/5985, 5986) used for remote command execution.

T1190.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
T1190.summary: Exploitation of web applications, e.g. SQL injection, file upload flaws leading to web shells.

T1071.name: Application Layer Protocol (C2)
T1071.summary: Command-and-control traffic blended into common protocols such as HTTPS; periodic beacons to an external host.

T1048.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
T1048.summary: Large or anomalous outbound transfers from internal hosts to external destinations.

T1078.name: Valid Accounts
T1078.summary: Use of a valid account, here: a successful login from a source that just produced a burst of failed logins.
